newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold closes up on Tokyo buying.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold closes up on Tokyo buying.

text.p: The Hong Kong gold market ended higher on buying from traders on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) as the dollar/yen rallied, dealers and traders said on Monday.
The dollar hit a 3-1/2 year high of 114.00 yen on Monday.
Shortcovering by Japanese banks in the gold market marked activity in Hong Kong bullion, but afternoon trade also saw buying interest from Europe, particularly Swiss buyers, gold traders noted.
"There were good offers from European buyers at around $383.50," said a bullion trader at an international bank.
Gold would remain range-bound between $382.50 and $384.00 gold traders said.
Bullion ended at US$383.00/383.50 an ounce Monday against New York's US$382.55/383.05 close on Friday.
Local gold ended HK$8 higher at HK$3,532 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to -1.00 from its previous level of -5.00
